newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans mixed, new crop down on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans mixed, new crop down on weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures opened mixed on Thursday with new crop months down on bearishly construed weather forecasts and nearbys up on USDA export data which came in above expectations, traders said.
The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook said U.S. Midwest temperatures from July 29 to August 2 would be normal to below normal with rainfall normal to above normal.
Soybeans were underpinned by the Census Bureau's June crush report which showed soy crushings at 108.89 million bushels, above an average of expectations for 108.5 million.
Export sales were mildly supportive for old crop.

USDA's weekly export sales report Thursday showed old crop soybean net export sales at 158,300 tonnes, above expectations for 75,000 to 125,000 tonnes. New crop net export sales totalled 423,800 tonnes, above expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
At 0955 CDT, soybeans were down four cents per bushel to up five cents with August up five at $7.44.
In opening trade, ADM and Dean Witter each bought one million bushels August while Continental Grain and Cargill Investor Services bought 0.5 million August. Refco Inc sold one million November.
